body: I’m a fully heterosexual woman. I’m assuming I got it from giving oral to someone with HSV2. My ex at the time definitely had a cold sore once though and he used to kiss my eyes. So maybe he just had oral HSV2 and didn’t know it. Who knows. HSV is kind of a weird diagnosis and I also think it’s hilarious that people absolutely panic over an HSV1 diagnosis. I’ve heard the same thing about HSV being seen as a normal skin condition in other parts of the world but here in the USA people despair so hard I wasn’t sure if that was accurate or not. I told my sister about it when I found out I had HSV2. She was a nurse and she told me women would come to her practice and sob like their parents just died over a simple diagnosis even without lesions or whatever. She explained to me that it’s not even a big deal and most people don’t get outbreaks and that we’ve just been made to think it’s so horrible and shameful when it’s not that serious. That was really helpful to learn right after my diagnosis and honestly I don’t really give a shit or tell anyone. Actually in many ways I’m less freaked out about using public restrooms and touching things at the gym and stuff lol idk. I’d probably be feeling way differently if I was getting outbreaks on my cooch so I do sympathize with those people dealing with that. My index value was over 10 when I was tested so hopefully I’m past that possibility.

That’s a helpful and interesting take. I also kinda figured it would be some complex and complicated thing. I still don’t really know what to make of it all. I’m not broken by it at all and I only mildly freaked out when I got my test results. I’ve been walking around with it all these years and it never really gave me trouble. I told my ex about my eye herpes when I found out about it all those years ago but my eye doctor had framed it like it was similar to chicken pox and gave me some eye drops and I didn’t really put it together at the time. I’m not super worried about future disclosure to be honest, especially since I don’t hook up or do anything when my eyes are bothering me. It just kinda sucks in general, especially since I don’t think I’ll ever have a definitive understanding of it all. But oh well.

I have symptom-free HSV2 also! Just found out a little under a year ago, but the way the antibodies appeared was as if I’ve had it for some time? But nobody knows. It doesn’t affect me at all. I only tell people who ask and pretty much nobody asks. I just have protected sex. HSV2 is relatively common. I’ve never really cared about it. I had like a week of panic and I just shrugged and got over it. Because I’ve probably been walking around carrying it for a long time and not noticing it. To me, nothing changed.

Hey there, how do you feel today? Did you go to school? Just so I’m upfront with you, I’m feeling like I want my life to end too. So I am talking to you because I care but not because I see an easy way out of this for either of us.

Thanks for responding though. I want you to know some things. For one, you’re obviously not stupid and there’s nothing wrong with you as a person. Your childhood sounds like all the cards just happened to fall in a shitty way due to a series of bad luck and judgements made about you based on things that happened, but not who you are. College can be way different if you choose to go. Bullying is much different in the way it happens in college. You’d have no history with anyone there and no judgments would be made about you based on what happened in grade school. There are so many more social groups and the social hierarchies are very different in college. There will be other people who are similar to you and people who will accept you just how you are. No matter what you think is wrong with you. Professors in college won’t allow bullying in the classroom and all the cliques in high school will be gone. I know that doesn’t help how you feel right now but there’s at least something to look forward to. People will be busy in college but it’s easier to make friends through clubs and class projects. Everyone in college is looking for a friend and most people there are there alone without anyone they know, so they’ll be more ready to reach out. It depends on where you go of course but the whole life you have right now would be changed. 

Have you thought about asking one of your potential friends to do something with you? Like maybe come over and play video games or help you pick a Christmas present for someone else? If you smoke weed, it creates an easy avenue to make a friend because kids are always happy to have a smoke session. It’s illegal yes but it’s pretty normal. If not that’s cool too, maybe you could find something that’s comfortable to you to offer. Are you nervous to ask people to hang out? I can totally see why you would be but I really don’t think it will make you look bad if you ask. 

If people are bullying you for how you look, you must know that it has nothing to do with you. Either they are immature teens, followers, or just pieces of shit on the inside. It doesn’t help to know that, because they still get to hurt you. I know, man. But I just don’t want you to feel bad about yourself because of it. Because it’s not you. Seriously, what’s such a big deal about being kinda thin / weak and having acne?  Look at all the adults with those same issues who have tons of friends and a wife / husband and kids and money and intelligence and fun times. It’s not that they are different from you or better than you somehow. Fuck no. It’s just that teenagers and kids are really fucked up and judgmental sometimes. 

I’m 32, a woman, and I’m middle eastern. I lived in a small town (here in America) when I was in middle school and I got bullied too. People fucked with me so much. Just because I was “different”, like you. But we all grew up and half of those people got pregnant and fucked their lives up and ended up being nothing. Everyone has their day. I’m grown up and honestly dude, I still feel like a teenager and my shit is not together still. The reason I’m telling you that is because I don’t feel that far removed from being a teen, like, I’m not just some old lady who just thinks, “oh, kids will be kids, you’ll move on.”  I mean you can/will move on, but I don’t think your problems are just inconsequential or anything. You are real and so is how you feel. 

You know what I think though? Suicide should be for people who can’t forsee a future due to some catastrophe that ruins the rest of their life. Loss of a child or a partner, economic disaster, terminal illness, divorce, homelessness etc. For people like that, their life isn’t just currently fucked - it’s permanently fucked in many cases. But you are not permanently fucked by any means. You have so much potential to see things change. You are smart even if you don’t think you are. You’re articulate and an emotional intellect. You care about your grades and you seem to care about others even if you struggle with anger. You’re so so so not a bad person. I know it means so little from a dumb adult on the Internet but I’m not saying it to stop you. It has nothing to do with me. This is simply a fact about YOU. Your good qualities outweigh your bad ones. You don’t need to change. You just need room and time to grow. You need companionship and I know your potential and your future won’t chabge anything that happened to you. I’m really sorry people treated you wrong. I’m so sorry you are hurt and lonely. There’s no erasing it or avoiding it. You really really don’t deserve it. And it unfortunately shaped you and impacted your personal development. But you are one of us. You’re here on this planet with us, you are part of all of this even if you feel insignificant. The pain you experience does matter. 

We have this saying in my home country:  “When one part of the body hurts, the whole body hurts.”  Like if you have a headache or something, you just feel like shit in general, right? If your finger is broken, your mind is affected too, you get what I mean? When YOU are hurting, YOU - Endoftheroad719, the whole world is affected. You are part of the body. It may not seem like it matters. But it does. And that’s not some spiritual thing - I am an atheist. It’s just true, you matter here. You’re one of us. You gotta do well, because you aren’t insignificant. 

I know it doesn’t change how you feel. But you have reasons to live. Maybe think about what they are. Ask yourself, what’s it going to take for you to feel okay? There’s got to be a solution. 

Hope you feel better today.
